claim: Static single-token hidden-state probes reach 0.90 AUROC and 0.96 F1 on LiveCodeBench in the best settings across four open-weight instruct LLMs, and richer dynamic token-selection or sequence models give no consistent gain.
stance_target: hidden states encode code correctness (L2 probe occupancy)
quoted_support: Static single-token probes perform best, reaching 0.90 AUROC and 0.96 F1 on LCB in the best settings, generally surpassing the thresholds of previously reported static probe baselines [40,4] for IUE. More elaborate dynamic token-selection and sequence-modeling strategies yield no consistent gains.

claim: Line-level fault localization with known-incorrect programs reaches a Top-3 hit rate of 81% in the best setting, while mixed-program line-level prediction is substantially harder.
quoted_support: in a conditional localization setup with known-incorrect programs, Top-K point-of-failure ranking remains effective, achieving a Top-3 hit rate of 81% in the best setting.

claim: The thesis forgoes strict contamination control: models were released after the LiveCodeBench cutoff and the author acknowledges possible contamination.
stance_target: L1 release-date contamination control is not done here
quoted_support: the methodology prioritizes compiling a large, diverse dataset of problems and responses over strict contamination control. Since this thesis uses models that were published after the benchmark's cutoff date, we recognize the possible impact of data contamination on model performance.

claim: A Qwen3-Coder single-token probe attains the highest Brier Skill Score on the CALIBRI test split, above the multicalibration baselines reported by Campos et al., but only for one model and one external benchmark.
stance_target: probe beats post-hoc calibration on code
quoted_support: our single-token probe achieves the highest BSS, significantly outperforming the strongest multicalibration baseline (IGLB).
